reason: The heaviest bills (rows 1, 2, 12) set a minimum share of women on Knesset candidate lists, and many others require adequate representation of women in public bodies (planning bodies, Chief Rabbinate electoral assembly, government companies, religious councils, civil service). The local-election and party-financing bills (rows 4, 6-8, 10, 13, 15, 16, 21, 23, 25, 40, about a quarter of the weight) use extra funding as an incentive rather than a hard requirement, but they push the same way; a voter who favors mandated minimum shares would favor them too. The statement fairly covers the bills; the price (parties dropping candidates their members chose) is honest for the main bills.
